Thanks again for taking the time this morning — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side:

2) Attachments: I attached a short spec that maps Redwood audit logging capabilities to common control families (redwood-audit-logging-spec.pdf).

3) Next steps (suggested):

Could you confirm the primary person on your side for the questionnaire and any compliance deadlines?

Marissa — thanks, helpful recap. A couple quick clarifying questions for the team before we start the questionnaire: 

- SOC 2: Is Redwood currently SOC 2 Type II certified, or is the SOC 2 in progress? If in progress, what timeline should we expect?

- Immutability: Can you confirm whether admin/API logs are append-only and whether we can export them in bulk (S3 / JSON) for our archival controls? Any retention limits?

Tom and I are also coordinating with our security procurement team; our deadline to complete the questionnaire is May 21.

Subject: Re: Acme - Audit logging capabilities & SOC 2 follow-up

Elena — thanks for the questions. Short answers below and attaching the SOC 2 summary.

- SOC 2: Redwood is currently SOC 2 Type II in-progress. We completed a readiness review Q4 2026 and expect Type II certification by Q3 2027. I attached our SOC 2 summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf) which includes scope and current control status.

- GDPR/HIPAA & BAA: We support enterprise deployments with customer-controlled data planes (Dedicated / Private) and can sign a BAA for covered deployments. For hosted accounts, we have controls around PII minimization and encryption; we can escalate to our legal/compliance team for a formal BAA conversation.

- Immutability & export: Our logging system writes append-only audit records for admin activity and API audit events. Exports can be delivered to customer S3 buckets (JSONL or Parquet) on a daily or on-demand basis; retention is configurable (default 90 days for hosted, longer for Dedicated/Private). For regulatory archives you can request longer retention windows and WORM-like configs for dedicated/private installs.

Next steps:
  - I’ll kick off the questionnaire responses and send initial answers by EOD tomorrow.
  - Aditya — can you add the export sample (1-day JSONL sample) and a short note on immutability guarantees?
  - Elena/Tom — if you can point me to your procurement contact or upload the completed questionnaire to the Drive link, we’ll prioritize answers.

Thanks,
Marissa

-- attachment: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (pdf)

Subject: Re: Acme - Audit logging capabilities & SOC 2 follow-up

Elena / team — adding the technical specifics as requested and attaching a 1-day export sample (sample-export-20270507.jsonl). Highlights: \

- Admin activity logs: include user id, action, resource, timestamp (ISO8601), IP address, request id, and before/after where applicable. Records are append-only and CRC checks are computed at write time.
- API request logs: per-request metadata plus payload hashes (no raw input unless customer enables request-body logging).
- Export formats: JSONL (line-delimited JSON), Parquet. Exports can be pushed to your S3 with server-side encryption.
- Retention & immutability: hosted defaults to 90 days; Dedicated/private deployments can configure retention up to multi-year and WORM-style configurations. For audit purposes we support signed manifests and checksums for exported bundles.

I attached the sample export for your security team to inspect. Happy to hop on a short call with your infra/security folks if they want to validate formats and export mechanics.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
